All notable changes to this project are documented here. The format follows
[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and the project uses
[Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html). How to cut a release is in
docs/DEVELOPMENT.md.

## [Unreleased]

## [1.5.0] - 2026-11-12

The editor now shows which `{{variables}}` will resolve, and edits an HTTP Request's
response mapping, headers and body as rows. One change for operators: the text log
format's separator (see Changed); `LOG_FORMAT=json`, which the monitoring profile reads,
is unchanged.

### Added

- **`{{variables}}` are coloured as you type**: green when the name resolves (a call
  field, a flow variable, a declared env var, or a name some component stores into), red
  with a wavy underline when nothing sets it, so it would be empty at run time. Hovering
  the field names the red ones. `/validate` now also returns `variables`, the names the
  flow's components store into.
- **HTTP Request's Response Mapping, Headers and Body are rows.** A mapping row is a
  path and the variable to save it as, with a one-click fix for a JSONPath or bracket
  path and a sample-JSON picker. Headers and Body are name → value rows with a
  Rows | JSON switch; a body holding a number, true/false, a list or a nested object
  opens as JSON. An empty body sends no body.

### Changed

- **HTTP Request's method sits before its URL**, on one line.
- **The component list shows no tooltip on hover.** The description is on the
  component's Properties pane.
- **The text log format separates the logger from the message with `: `** (was an em
  dash): `INFO     app.audit: …`. `LOG_FORMAT=json` is unchanged. Anything that parses
  the text format by that separator needs the new one.
- **No em-dashes in the app's messages, UI or docs.** Log, error and validation
  messages keep their wording; only the punctuation around each dash changed. A missing
  timestamp shows `-`, and an empty dropdown choice reads `(none)`.
- **Dependencies** (development and monitoring only): the build stage's uv image
  (digest e80c05a3), CI's `setup-uv` v10.3.3 (was v10.3.2), and the monitoring
  profile's Prometheus v3.16.0 (was v3.15.1). The app's own Python dependencies are
  unchanged.

## [1.4.2] - 2026-11-10

A security update: oauthlib moves to the release that actually closes the advisory 1.4.1
was cut for, and the runtime image's base is refreshed. The `v1.4.1` tag's image scan
failed on both, so upgrade from 1.3.1 straight to 1.4.2; 1.4.0's notes below apply.
The scan now also runs weekly, so the next such advisory is noticed without a push.

### Security

- **oauthlib 4.0.1** (was 4.0.0; [CVE-2026-49272](https://avd.aquasec.com/nvd/cve-2026-49272),
  HIGH). 1.4.1 moved to 4.0.0 for this advisory, but its fix is in 4.0.1 (the advisory
  names `< 4.0.1`; 4.0.0 closed a different one). python-fasthtml requires oauthlib for
  its OAuth sign-in, which this app doesn't use.

- **The runtime base image is refreshed** (`python:3.14-slim-trixie`, built
  2026-11-08): `apt` 3.0.4 ([CVE-2026-109518](https://avd.aquasec.com/nvd/cve-2026-109518),
  HIGH; the image runs no apt, but the scan reported it). The same image still ships
  `zlib1g` 1:1.3.dfsg+really1.3.1-1+b1, which Debian has fixed
  ([DSA-6613-1](https://www.debian.org/security/2026/dsa-6613):
  [CVE-2026-76844](https://avd.aquasec.com/nvd/cve-2026-76844),
  [CVE-2026-85091](https://avd.aquasec.com/nvd/cve-2026-85091), both HIGH; heap
  overflows in zlib's `gz*` file-writing routines, which nothing in the image calls)
  but no rebuilt base image carries yet; the Dockerfile runs no apt to pick it up. Those
  two are listed in a root `.trivyignore` with an expiry of 2026-12-15, so the scan is
  green until the base image is rebuilt (the next release takes the digest bump) and
  red again on that date if it isn't.

### Added

- **A weekly image scan** (`.github/workflows/image-scan.yml`, development only): the
  same Trivy scan CI runs on every push, run against `master` every Monday (and from
  the Actions tab), so a CVE published against a base image or a locked dependency is
  noticed on the released image without waiting for the next push. See
  docs/DEVELOPMENT.md.

### Changed

- **Dependencies**: python-fasthtml 0.14.17 (was 0.14.13), starlette 1.10.0 (was
  1.7.0), anyio 4.16.0 (was 4.15.1), pydantic 2.14.2 (was 2.14.1). The monitoring
  profile's images: Loki 3.7.9, Prometheus v3.15.1, Alloy v1.21.3, Grafana 13.3.0.
  Development: playwright 1.64.1, pytest 9.2.0, pytest-mock 3.17.0, ruff 0.17.3 (the
  lint's rule set is unchanged), and the build stage's uv image and CI's `setup-uv`
  (v10.3.2) pins.
- **Docs:** `AGENTS.md`, the guide for contributors and coding agents, is now a short
  core (about 21 KB, was 179 KB); the full facts and reasoning moved, unchanged, to
  `docs/internals/` (ten files, one per subsystem).

## [1.4.1] - 2026-10-30

A security update: oauthlib, which the web framework requires, moves past a HIGH
advisory. The `v1.4.0` tag's image scan failed on it, so upgrade from 1.3.1 straight to
1.4.1; 1.4.0's notes below apply.

### Security

- **oauthlib 4.0.0** (was 3.3.1; [CVE-2026-49272](https://avd.aquasec.com/nvd/cve-2026-49272),
  HIGH). python-fasthtml requires it for its OAuth sign-in, which this app doesn't use;
  the image scan of the `v1.4.0` tag failed on it.

## [1.4.0] - 2026-10-30

The Jambonz SDK moves to 0.4.0, and its builder now writes and checks every verb: the
verbs sent to Jambonz carry the SDK's defaults and spelling, and a save refuses what the
SDK rejects, on the component that holds it. Read the upgrade notes: a flow holding such
a value keeps running as it was compiled before, until it is fixed.

### Changed

- **jambonz-python-sdk 0.4.0** (was 0.3.2), and every verb is now built and checked by
  its builder, so what reaches Jambonz is what the SDK (made for the commercial
  Jambonz) writes. The verbs change on the wire: they carry the SDK's defaults (a
  gather's `listenDuringPrompt: true`, a Transfer target's `method: "POST"`, a Record's
  `sampleRate: 8000`, an AI Agent's `cancelOnBargeIn` / `cancelOnResponseTimeout:
  false`), a gather's prompt is written `{"verb": "say", …}`, numbers are written as
  decimals (`8.0`), and an ElevenLabs AI Agent's `auth.api_key` is sent as `apiKey`.

- **A save refuses a value the SDK rejects, on the component that holds it**: an
  unknown field, a value outside a list of choices, text where a number belongs. The
  Issues row names the field and jumps to the component; it never repeats the value.

- **Compiled flows are rebuilt once after the upgrade** (`COMPILED_FORMAT_VERSION` 4:
  the verbs above). It happens on each flow's first call, automatically.

- **A component card's name has no tooltip.** It is the card's own text, and the
  Properties pane's Label field shows it in full; the summary line under it keeps its
  tooltip with the full text.

### Upgrade notes

- **A flow with a value the SDK now rejects keeps running as compiled before.** Each
  flow is recompiled on its first call; one that no longer compiles is served from its
  previous compiled form, with an ERROR in the log naming the flow, until the component
  is fixed and the flow saved. Open each flow after upgrading: its Issues tab lists what
  to fix.
- **The verbs sent to Jambonz change** (see Changed). Place a test call through your
  flows' Menus, User Inputs, Transfers and AI Agents before relying on it.

## [1.3.1] - 2026-10-23

A security update: the CA bundle the HTTP Request node verifies TLS against no longer
trusts emSign's compromised intermediates. The `v1.3.0` tag's image scan failed on
that advisory, so upgrade from 1.2.0 straight to 1.3.1; 1.3.0's notes below apply.

### Security

- **The CA bundle no longer trusts emSign's compromised intermediates.** `certifi`
  2026.10.19 (was 2026.5.20; [GHSA-6q48-6c7w-9gw2](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6q48-6c7w-9gw2)),
  the bundle the HTTP Request node verifies an API's TLS certificate against. The
  advisory appeared after 1.3.0 was cut, and the image scan of the `v1.3.0` tag failed on
  it.

## [1.3.0] - 2026-10-23

Where callers go, on the dashboard; a load test for sizing how many webhooks run at
once, which now defaults to 100; pages that run no inline script; and browser tests for
the editor. Read the upgrade notes: an `.env` made from an earlier `.env.example` keeps
the old limit of 40, and a script a proxy injects into the pages is now refused.

### Added

- **Browser tests for the editor** (development only). `tests/browser/` drives the real
  app in Chromium with Playwright (sign-in, every main page, placing and editing
  components, Deploy, Issues, undo/redo, Simulate, the live Debug feed, the confirm
  dialog, the read-only account) and fails a test on any console error, failed request
  or Content-Security-Policy violation. Run with `uv run pytest -m browser` (left out of
  the default run); CI runs it in a new `browser` job, and the pre-push hook where
  Chromium is installed. See docs/DEVELOPMENT.md, "The browser suite".

- **Where callers go, on the dashboard.** Every routing decision is now an INFO line on
  the `app.routing` logger (`waiting` when a hook leaves the call waiting at a Menu,
  User Input, Transfer, queue or other component that waits for an answer, `routed`
  when that answer is routed or a Conditional or Date & Time picks its branch), naming
  the component (id, type, label), what happened (`result`: the option pressed,
  `timeout`, `invalid`, a transfer's `failure`, a queue's `hangup`, the rule that
  matched) and the branch the call took (`outlet`). Never the digits, speech or numbers
  themselves, and nothing from a dry run. The Grafana dashboard gets a Routing row
  drawn from them: *Where callers go* (decisions per component and outlet) and *Hung up
  while waiting* (calls that waited at a component and never came back), with a Flow
  box to narrow it to one flow. About one or two more log lines per webhook. See
  docs/OPERATIONS.md, "Reading the Routing panels".

- **A load test for sizing `WEBHOOK_MAX_CONCURRENCY`.** `scripts/load_test.py` plays
  Jambonz at your own instance: whole calls (inbound hook, each continuation, status
  events) with Jambonz's payloads, signature and customerData echo, arriving at a rate
  you set or ramp, against a bundled flow (`scripts/load_test_flow.json`, `--import`)
  whose HTTP lookup calls a built-in upstream you can slow down (`--upstream-delay`). It
  reports per step and hook kind (latency percentiles, shed hooks, late and failed
  answers), says whether the slots or the process's CPU ran out first and how many slots
  the flow needs (Erlang B), and exits non-zero past `--max-failed-pct`. See
  docs/OPERATIONS.md, "Capacity and sizing".
- **Shed webhook answers carry `X-Jamhooks-Shed: 1`**, whatever their status, so a load
  test or a proxy log can count them without matching `CALLER_BUSY_MESSAGE` (which may be
  localised, or empty).

### Security

- **The pages no longer allow inline script: the CSP's `script-src` is `'self'`.** It
  allowed `'unsafe-inline'` for the editor's inlined code and a few `onclick` handlers,
  which left escaping as the only thing between a flow's text and script running in the
  editor of whoever opened it. Now a browser runs only script files the app serves: the
  editor, the theme switch, the dashboard menus and the New / Import page are files under
  `/static`, and the data a page needs travels in `<script type="application/json">`
  blocks, which never execute. See docs/HARDENING.md.

### Changed

- **Script and stylesheet URLs carry a `?v=` content hash**, so after an upgrade a browser
  fetches the new editor instead of running a cached one against the new server.
  Something in front of the app that injects a script of its own (an analytics snippet,
  a banner) must now serve it as a file, or the browser refuses it.

- **Compiled flows are rebuilt once after the upgrade** (`COMPILED_FORMAT_VERSION` 3:
  a compiled component now carries its label, for the routing lines). It happens on each
  flow's first call, automatically; nothing to do.

- **`WEBHOOK_MAX_CONCURRENCY` defaults to 100** (was 40, anyio's own default, never
  measured). The load test showed what a slot spends its time on: waiting for an HTTP
  Request's API. With a 2 s API, 40 slots turned callers away at about half the rate one
  core could serve, and 100 ran clean up to that limit. A waiting slot costs one idle
  thread, and `MAX_HOOK_SECONDS` still bounds how long it waits.

### Fixed

- **The webhook-name fields checked nothing** (on the New tab and when renaming in the
  editor's Details pane). Their pattern was not a valid regular expression for current
  browsers, which dropped the check and logged a console error.

- The dashboard's *Calls by flow* table titles its count column *Calls* (it showed
  Grafana's `Value #A`).

### Upgrade notes

- **An `.env` made from an earlier `.env.example` keeps `WEBHOOK_MAX_CONCURRENCY=40`**:
  the line sets it, so the new default doesn't reach you. Change it to `100` (or to what
  `scripts/load_test.py` says your flows need) and run `docker compose up -d`.
- **A script injected into the pages by something in front of the app is now refused**
  by the browser (the CSP allows only the app's own files): an analytics snippet or a
  banner added by a proxy has to be served as a file instead. The app's own pages are
  unaffected.

## [1.2.0] - 2026-10-20

Monitoring with logs kept for 30 days, test benches that exercise every component on a
real call, and the project's new name, Jamhooks. Read the upgrade notes before moving
or re-cloning a checkout: Compose names the store volume after its directory.

### Added

- **Monitoring, with logs kept for 30 days.** A `monitoring` compose profile (Loki,
  Grafana Alloy, Prometheus and Grafana) keeps the app's log lines for `LOG_RETENTION`
  (30 days by default) and then deletes them, probes `/health`, and comes with a
  dashboard (calls, webhook latency and outcomes, calls per flow, `/health`, the log
  with a call-sid search, the audit trail) and nine alert rules (app unreachable,
  webhooks shed, failing or slow, unknown flows, store unwritable, sign-in paused, an
  unsafe configuration at start, any other error). `scripts/check_monitoring.py` checks
  a running stack; CI starts it on every change. See docs/OPERATIONS.md, "Monitoring".
- **Node test benches.** Seven example flows (`example/nodes/…`, in the Load Example tab)
  that use every component between them: prompts and call audio, caller input, data
  tools, queues and conference, transfers and SMS, streaming and AI, subflow calls. Each
  is a keypad menu: a key runs one test, says which outlet it took and returns to the
  menu; destinations and services come from env vars set in the portal. See
  docs/FLOWS.md, "Trying every component on a real call".

### Changed

- **The project is now called Jamhooks.** The repository moved to
  `github.com/jamhooks/jamhooks` (the old URL redirects), the image is `jamhooks:<version>`
  and the editor's page titles and sign-in page say Jamhooks. Flows, webhook URLs,
  settings and sign-ins are unchanged. The `ivr-app-unreachable` alert is now titled
  *Jamhooks unreachable*.
- **Docs:** the README is now an overview and a quick start. The reference it held moved
  to `docs/`: building flows (`FLOWS.md`), how calls run (`RUNTIME.md`), the API
  (`API.md`), every setting (`CONFIGURATION.md`), production setup (`DEPLOYMENT.md`),
  security hardening (`HARDENING.md`) and development and releasing (`DEVELOPMENT.md`).

### Upgrade notes

- **Keep your checkout's directory, or name the project.** Compose names the volumes
  after the directory (`<directory>_storedata` holds every flow), so a checkout moved to,
  or freshly cloned into, a directory called `jamhooks` starts with an **empty store**.
  Update an existing checkout in place (`git remote set-url origin
  https://github.com/jamhooks/jamhooks.git`, then upgrade as usual), or set
  `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME` in `.env` to the old directory's name before the first
  `docker compose up` in the new place. `docker volume ls` shows which name holds yours.
- The new release builds `jamhooks:<version>`. Earlier releases' images keep the name
  they were built under, and a rollback to one still finds it: the compose file at that
  release's tag names it.
- A browser that signed in before the upgrade is a stranger to the sign-in throttle
  again until its next successful sign-in (the known-browser cookie is signed under the
  new name). Only matters while sign-in is paused for strangers; sessions are unaffected.
- `.env.example` now turns the profile on (`COMPOSE_PROFILES=monitoring`) and sets
  `LOG_FORMAT=json`, which the dashboard and alerts read. An existing `.env` is
  unchanged: add those two lines and a `GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD` to get the stack, then
  set up where alerts go in Grafana (Alerting → Contact points). Without them nothing
  changes; the app still runs alone.

## [1.1.0] - 2026-10-15

The Logger can also raise its line as a Jambonz alert. Nothing to do on upgrade:
the option is off on every existing Logger, and stored flows run as before.

### Added

- **The Logger can also raise a Jambonz alert.** Tick *Also send to Jambonz Alerts page*
  and the line it logs is also raised as an application alert, listed against the call
  on the Jambonz portal's Alerts page. Jambonz ignores what the call-status hook returns,
  so the save refuses it ticked in the Disconnect and Call Status handlers and anywhere
  they lead (a Logger that only logs stays allowed there), and in a queue's wait subflow.

## [1.0.1] - 2026-10-14

Fixes from an audit of 1.0.0: one routing bug that callers hear, call state that went
missing at the edges, webhook URLs that broke on a trailing slash, and operator docs
that were wrong.

### Upgrade notes

- **User Input with an `invalid` branch now routes valid answers correctly.** A valid
  answer used to play the `invalid` branch first. It now takes `default`, or the next
  component. If a flow worked around this, review it.
- **`ALLOWED_HOSTS` entries keep their port for the cross-site checks.** A bare name
  means the standard port (`https://name` or `http://name`), and `name:8443` means that
  port only. Only a proxy that rewrites `Host` *and* serves the editor on a
  non-standard port needs a change: list it as `name:port`. Otherwise browsers that
  don't send `Sec-Fetch-Site` get 403 on saves and the Debug pane won't attach. An
  invalid port in an entry is now warned about and the entry ignored.
- **Don't restart on an unhealthy `/health`.** If you followed the old advice (a cron or
  systemd restart, `autoheal`, a Kubernetes liveness probe on `/health`), remove it: a
  restart drops every live call and fixes none of the causes. Use `/health` to alert a
  human. A liveness check, if you want one, is a TCP check on the port. See
  [OPERATIONS.md](/reference/operations/).
- **A response that ends the call may now carry a `tag` verb.** It holds the call's
  variables for the Disconnect and Call Status handlers. Tooling that asserts exact verb
  lists will see it.

### Fixed

- **User Input sent valid answers down `invalid`** when that branch was wired.
- **The Disconnect and Call Status handlers saw stale variables.** A variable set after
  the last menu or input step (say, the department chosen before a goodbye) never reached
  them; on a call that never suspended, none did.
- **An Error handler that waited for input forgot this hook's variables**: the Start
  values, `http_error` and HTTP Request mappings, so a "press 1 to retry" lost them.
- **A deleted flow variable came back** with its default after the next menu or input
  step.
- **Change Variable's replace with an empty search text** inserted the replacement
  between every character, and the value grew on every loop pass. It now changes
  nothing, and a blank search text is a save warning.
- **JSON nested too deep to parse** sent the call to the Error handler from a JSON
  Parser. It now sets `{{json_error}}`, and an HTTP Request sets `{{http_error}}` with a
  clean message.
- **A queue's wait hook answered say + hangup when shed or unrenderable**, which Jambonz
  refuses: the queued caller sat in silence, under load. It now answers with nothing to
  play.
- **A trailing `/` on a webhook URL broke every call** ("unavailable"), hid the env vars
  from the portal, and sent `/callstatus/` and `/subflows/<name>/` to the inbound route.
  Every hook now answers on its URL with one trailing slash.
- **The image shipped without `examples/`**, so Load Example was empty in production.
- **A deeply nested JSON body to `/api/` was a 500.** It is now a 400.

### Security

- **A page on another port of a listed `ALLOWED_HOSTS` name passed the CSRF and
  Debug-socket origin checks**, so it could delete flows or watch live calls.
- **Dynamic responses are `Cache-Control: no-store`**, so a browser can't keep the
  admin's editor page (obscure defaults in clear) past a sign-out on a shared machine.

### Documentation

- **`/health` docs.** A full disk is a 503, and the probe is for alerting only.
- **The nginx example passes `nginx -t` on Ubuntu 24.04 and Debian 12**
  (`listen 443 ssl http2;`).
- **README corrections:** the handler JSON keys are `error`, `disconnect` and
  `callstatus`; the Debug pane section is rewritten; backups stop the app first; the
  proxy-address steps run in an order that works; webhook basic auth goes on both
  webhooks.

## [1.0.0] - 2026-10-13

The first tagged release. It gathers two production-readiness passes: the second checked
the runtime against what a real Jambonz sends (its feature-server source and the SDK's
callback schemas) rather than against this app's own assumptions, and fixed what didn't
match.

### Upgrade notes

Read these before deploying this release over an existing one.

- **Configure the call status webhook.** A Jambonz application has two webhooks; point
  the *call status webhook* at `…/webhooks/<flow>/callstatus`. The Disconnect and Call
  Status handlers run only from it; Jambonz has no error or disconnect hook. Remove any
  status hook pointed at `/error` or `/disconnect`.
- **A hook answers within 8 s.** `MAX_HOOK_SECONDS` defaults to 8 (was 30), because
  Jambonz waits about 10 s for an answer and doesn't retry. An HTTP Request gets at most
  what is left of the hook's budget, and the Error handler runs on the remainder. A flow
  whose hooks legitimately took longer now ends in its Error handler; raising the setting
  above ~9 s is pointless.
- **Components after a Subflow node now run** when the subflow ends; they were dead
  before. Review flows that left anything there.
- **Saves are stricter.** Deployed flows keep running from their last compiled artifact,
  with an `ERROR` naming them, until they are fixed and saved. Refused now: a cycle
  through a Subflow, or through a Loop entered from outside its body; Send SMS in the
  Disconnect or Call Status handler; a variable named `reason`, `queue_result`,
  `dequeue_result`, `refer_status` or `final_referred_call_status`, or any name starting
  with `__` (the runtime's own); Call Control or Send SMS reached from the Disconnect or
  Call Status handler through a Subflow component or a Connector; a queue's wait subflow that plays
  anything but play/say/pause/tag/leave; a template condition that doesn't
  parse; an unknown Date/Time timezone; an AI Agent with an unsupported vendor or without
  its vendor's required keys.
- **Running flows behave differently where they were wrong:**
  - template conditions with an operator evaluate as written (`{{x}} == 'y'` was always
    true);
  - a numeric comparison on an unset or empty variable is no longer satisfied (it read
    as 0): initialise counters before testing them;
  - a blank Date/Time timezone is UTC (it was the host's local time), and an overnight
    window covers the morning *after* the day it starts;
  - Play Prompt with loop 0 repeats until interrupted, and a voice, language or gender
    set without a vendor is now used (with the call's vendor) instead of ignored;
  - a successful Blind Transfer ends the flow: the components after it run only when it
    failed;
  - a Take From Queue `bridged` branch routes as `complete`, and an Enter Queue `timeout`
    or Take From Queue `error` branch is flagged as one that can never be taken;
  - Voice Input and Transcribe left blank inherit the application's speech settings;
    existing components keep the google/en-US they were created with until cleared;
  - an AI Agent with a system prompt and key but no model options is moved into its
    vendor's template; any other old configuration fails to save, with directions;
  - a variable whose name starts with `__` no longer survives a wait for input: rename it.
- **Compiled artifacts are rebuilt on first use** (format 2). Nothing to do.
- **Reverse proxy:** if you copied the nginx example, change it to
  `proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $remote_addr;` and set `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS` to the
  proxy's address, never `*`.
- **Obscure env-var defaults stay in the app:** exports and version downloads drop them
  (importing one leaves the default empty), the read-only account sees `••••••••`, and
  Simulate shows `[redacted]`. Secrets belong in the Jambonz portal.
- **Docker:** the image is now tagged with its release version; the old
  `<project>-app:latest` is left alone as your rollback target. It runs Python 3.14 on
  Debian 13 with a read-only root filesystem. Build with
  `--build-arg APP_REVISION="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"` so it can report its revision. Back
  up with `scripts/backup.sh` and restore with `scripts/restore.sh`; the old copy-paste
  commands couldn't read the session key.
- **Store files are owner-only** (0600), tightened on their next write.
- **Logs:** timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC with milliseconds (`…Z`); uvicorn's own lines now
  follow `LOG_FORMAT` and `LOG_LEVEL` and go to stderr; control characters are escaped
  (`\x0a`). `/health` can answer 503 on a full volume, and its body carries `version`.
- **SSRF guard** (`HTTP_REQUEST_ALLOW_PRIVATE=false`): 100.64.0.0/10 is refused, and a
  public host reached through NAT64 (`64:ff9b::/96`) is allowed.
- **New warnings** (they never block a save): an obscure env var with a default; a Send SMS
  recipient the caller controls; a variable named like a field Jambonz sends; a blank
  Date/Time timezone; a literal API key in an AI Agent.

- **Everyone signs in once.** Sessions now carry a sign-in time and a session id; a
  cookie from before the upgrade has neither and is refused.
- **Every compiled flow is rebuilt on its first call** (a new format stamp). A flow the
  stricter validation below now refuses keeps answering from its previous compiled
  artifact, with an `ERROR` naming it, until it is fixed and saved. Check the log after
  the upgrade.
- **Saves are stricter.** A save is refused (422 with issues) when the flow would not
  compile (including the Jambonz verb-schema checks the save used to skip) and when it
  uses a reserved variable name (`digits`, `speech`, `queueResult`, `dial_call_status`, …)
  or a component id / subflow name outside `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`.
- **HTTP Request URLs are percent-encoded.** Values interpolated into the path, query or
  fragment are encoded; a placeholder that starts the URL or sits in the host part is
  not. Write `{{var|raw}}` where a mid-URL value must go in as-is. Where a URL starts
  with a base placeholder, its *value* decides where the host part ends: with no path in
  it (`https://api.example.com`), `{{BASE}}{{path}}` inserts `{{path}}` as-is; with one,
  what follows is encoded. A save now **warns** about a placeholder that is a whole query
  component (`?{{qs}}`: a pre-built `a=1&b=2` is sent encoded as one value) and about a
  placeholder in a Change Variable regex (matched literally now). Check the Issues tab
  of flows that use either.
- **Values that used to be ignored now apply** (see the compose fix below), and an
  invalid number (negative, `nan`, a typo) now falls back to its default with a warning:
  a negative `MAX_HOOK_SECONDS` no longer disables the budget, and a
  `WEBHOOK_MAX_CONCURRENCY` below 1 becomes 40, not 1.
- **An editor without a login answers only on loopback names and the `BASE_WEBHOOK_URL`
  host.** Reached another way (an IP, an internal name)? Set `ALLOWED_HOSTS`.
- **`/api/` writes with a body must be `application/json`** (anything else is a 415).
- **Compose publishes the port on `127.0.0.1` only.** If Jambonz (or a proxy on another
  host) reaches port 5001 directly, set `APP_PUBLISH=5001` before `up -d`, or every
  webhook stops arriving. The compose file now needs **Docker Compose 2.24 or later**
  (`env_file` with `required: false`).
- **`HTTP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT` is a total deadline** for the whole request, body included,
  not a per-read timeout; an API that is slow but steady may need a higher value.
- **Call state is capped at `MAX_CALL_STATE_BYTES` (64 KiB).** A flow that stores a
  large HTTP response in a variable now runs its Error handler at the next wait for
  input, rather than having Jambonz's next webhook refused; map the fields you need.

### Added

- **Subflows call and return.** When a subflow ends (right away or after menus and
  transfers), the call continues after the Subflow node. One subflow can be used from
  many places, calls nest, and recursion is refused at save.
- **Template conditions are expressions:** `==` `!=` `<` `>` `<=` `>=` `contains`,
  `and`/`or`/`not` and parentheses, parsed before any value is filled in: caller input
  can't become syntax. A template that doesn't parse is reported at save.
- **AI Agent starter templates** for every vendor Jambonz's `llm` verb supports (openai,
  microsoft, google, deepgram, voiceagent, ultravox, elevenlabs), in its own editor panel.
  Each vendor's required keys are checked at save, and the API key's env var is declared
  obscure automatically.
- **Per-prompt voice** (vendor, language, voice) on Menu, User Input and Voice Input.
- **An `invalid` outlet on User Input**, for fewer digits than its minimum.
- **`CALLER_UNAVAILABLE_MESSAGE` and `CALLER_BUSY_MESSAGE`**: what a caller hears when
  the flow can't run or the app is busy (empty hangs up without a word).
- **Version reporting:** `/health` and a startup line carry the version and the build's
  `APP_REVISION`; the image carries OCI labels.
- **`scripts/backup.sh` and `scripts/restore.sh`**, run by CI against the built image.
- **CI on `v*` tags** builds, scans and smoke-tests the image and checks that
  `pyproject.toml`, `docker-compose.yml` and this changelog name the same version
  (nothing is published).
- **A versioned pre-push hook:** `git config core.hooksPath scripts/git-hooks`.
- **The release check covers `uv.lock`:** a test and the tag's CI job fail unless
  `pyproject.toml`, the compose image tag, its `APP_VERSION` and `uv.lock` name the same
  version.
- **Contract tests built from the Jambonz SDK's callback schemas**, so the runtime is
  checked against what Jambonz sends, not against its own assumptions.
- **Save warnings:** an obscure env var with a default; a Send SMS recipient the caller
  controls (SMS pumping); a variable named like a field Jambonz sends; a blank Date/Time
  timezone.
- **Date/Time components take the browser's timezone** when they are added.
- **CI:** a container smoke test: the built image is started with login and a webhook
  secret, and must answer `/health` and `/login`, log no `SECURITY:` line, and stop
  cleanly on `SIGTERM`.
- **CI:** a Trivy scan of the image, failing on fixable HIGH/CRITICAL vulnerabilities.
- **CI:** Dependabot (weekly grouped updates for the GitHub Actions, the base images
  and the Python lock).
- **CI:** `tests/test_deploy_config.py` (`.env` reaches the container, compose pins
  nothing beyond its allowed set, every setting the app reads is documented in
  `.env.example`, and the shutdown timeouts nest).
- **Docs:** `docs/OPERATIONS.md` (Caddy and nginx examples, backup and restore, upgrade
  and rollback, secret rotation, and why it is one instance per store).
- **Docs:** `docs/PRIVACY.md` (what the app stores and logs about callers and editor
  users).
- **Docs:** a Releasing section in the README, and this changelog.
- **Audit trail:** one `app.audit` line per change to a flow (create, save, rename,
  restore, import, duplicate, delete) naming the account or gateway identity, the flow
  and its version; every version snapshot records its author, shown in the history.
- **A completion line per webhook**: status, `duration_ms`, verb count and outcome flags
  (`shed`, `not_found`, `node_error`, `error_handler`, `budget_exceeded`,
  `render_failed`); top-level keys under `LOG_FORMAT=json`, and the source for metrics.
- **Settings:** `MAX_CALL_STATE_BYTES` (64 KiB), `ALLOWED_HOSTS`, `SESSION_MAX_LIFETIME`
  (12 h), `TRUSTED_USER_HEADER_SECRET`.
- **`CONFIG:` startup errors** for a missing or loopback `BASE_WEBHOOK_URL` on a public
  bind, and warnings for every setting that is invalid and fell back to its default.
- **`{{var|raw}}`**: opt a value out of URL encoding (and of regex escaping).
- **A compiler warning** when a Transfer or Blind Transfer target is built from caller
  input (`{{digits}}`, `{{from}}`, a gathered variable…). Check it with a Conditional
  first, or it is a toll-fraud path.

### Changed

- **`MAX_HOOK_SECONDS` 30 → 8**, HTTP Request deadlines clamped to what is left of the
  hook's budget, and the Error handler run on the remainder: every hook answers inside
  Jambonz's ~10 s wait.
- **The Disconnect handler runs from the call status webhook**, once, on the call's final
  status; **the Call Status handler runs only for the leg the flow drives**. The Details
  page lists the two webhooks Jambonz has, and which webhook auth is on.
- **Loops, Connectors and Exit:** a Loop entered from outside its body restarts its count;
  a Connector into another tree abandons any subflow calls in progress; Exit Call Flow
  inside a subflow ends the call.
- **A compare condition's value may be `{{var}}`.**
- **Speech recognition left blank inherits the application's settings** (it used to force
  google/en-US).
- **A successful Blind Transfer ends the flow.**
- **`OPTIONS` (env-var discovery) is exempt from webhook basic auth** (Jambonz sends no
  credentials on it) and answers 204 for a flow without env vars.
- **`/health` proves a real write**; logs are one format end to end, with UTC millisecond
  timestamps.
- **Docker:** Python 3.14 on Debian 13, a read-only root filesystem, root-owned source
  byte-compiled at build time, an allowlist build context and one image tag per release. **CI:** Python 3.11–3.14 on
  `ubuntu-24.04`, `uv --locked`, ruff's rules selected explicitly; dependency floors raised
  to what the code relies on, and `starlette`, `anyio` and `httpcore` declared.
- **Deployment:** compose publishes the port on `127.0.0.1` only; a reverse proxy on the
  same host still reaches it. Set `APP_PUBLISH=5001` (or `0.0.0.0:5001`) to publish it
  on every interface as before.
- **Deployment:** container logs are capped at 5 × 10 MB (they carry call sids and the
  addresses of failed sign-ins).
- **Deployment:** both Dockerfile base images are pinned by digest, and pip, setuptools
  and wheel are removed from the runtime image (unused there; setuptools carried
  vulnerable vendored packages).
- **CI:** every action is pinned to a commit SHA and moved to its current major
  (Node 24): `actions/checkout` v7, `astral-sh/setup-uv` v10, `actions/setup-node` v7.
  Workflows run with a read-only token and don't persist checkout credentials.
- **UI assets:** Font Awesome 7.3.1 (was 6.5.1) and htmx 2.0.11 (was 1.9.12). Font
  Awesome 7 ships woff2 webfonts only, so the old `.ttf` files are deleted from
  `vendor/` on the first start after the upgrade, and icons are fixed-width by default
  (a few are a little wider). htmx 4 is out but npm still tags it `next`, and FastHTML
  targets htmx 2.

### Security

- **The documented reverse-proxy setup let a client choose its own address**, escaping
  the per-address rate limit and sign-in lockout. nginx now overwrites `X-Forwarded-For`,
  `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS` names the proxy, and both per-address maps are capped.
- **Obscure env-var defaults** are masked for the read-only account and dropped from
  exports, version downloads and Simulate output.
- **Env-var values are read only from a call's first hook**, and with webhook auth off the
  startup error now says that anyone can set them, and so steer where an HTTP Request
  sends its secrets.
- **SSRF guard:** every non-global address is refused, including 100.64.0.0/10 (cloud
  metadata, Tailscale); a NAT64 address is judged by the IPv4 address it reaches.
- **Log lines can't be forged** with newlines or control characters, in either format.
- **The runtime's own state can't be forged:** names starting with `__` are reserved, a
  hook body can't set one, and a call-stack entry that isn't a Subflow node of the
  deployed flow is dropped; with webhook auth off, a forged one could resume a call
  wherever it liked.
- **Caller-facing fallback messages no longer reveal internals** ("Flow not found or not
  compiled.").
- **Owner-only storage:** store files 0600 and directories 0700, backups 0600; the
  container's root filesystem is read-only and its source root-owned.
- **Closed an arbitrary file read.** FastHTML's catch-all static route served any file on
  the host with a common extension (`.txt`, `.yml`, `.csv`, `.zip`, …) through `..` in
  the path, to anyone when the editor had no login, to any signed-in account
  otherwise. The route is removed; assets are served by the `/static` mounts.
- **Caller data and secrets kept out of the logs.** The HTTP client's per-request INFO
  line (full URL, query string included: the caller's number, the API key) is off,
  and an HTTP Request failure logs the host it went to and the path as the author wrote
  it (`/accounts/{{digits}}`): no interpolated caller input, no query string.
- **Secret (*obscure*) environment variables** no longer appear as defaults in the
  `OPTIONS` schema answer and are masked in the Debug pane.
- **Caller input can't reshape requests:** URL values are percent-encoded (above), and a
  Change Variable regex escapes interpolated values instead of compiling them.
- **CSRF:** an `Origin: null` (sandboxed frame) no longer passes the origin check, and a
  cross-site `text/plain` body can no longer reach the JSON API.
- **DNS rebinding:** see `ALLOWED_HOSTS`. The Debug socket also checks `Origin` (close
  code 4400).
- **Trusted-header mode** can require a shared secret from the gateway
  (`TRUSTED_USER_HEADER_SECRET`), and a startup warning says when it doesn't.
- **Sessions:** a 12-hour absolute lifetime, and signing out revokes the session on the
  server, not just in the browser. `.sesskey` is created `0600`.
- **Less leaked:** `/health` no longer returns the store path on failure; a failed
  sign-in no longer logs the typed username.
- **Webhooks:** a malformed signature is a 403, not a 500; `OPTIONS` runs in its own
  two-slot lane so a flood of them can't take every call slot.
- **Front-end assets are pinned to exact versions and verified by sha256.** Tailwind
  was pinned only to its major (`@4`, whatever the CDN served that day); it is now
  4.3.3, fetched as the npm package's own file rather than jsDelivr's on-the-fly
  re-minification. Every file the app vendors (Tailwind, HTMX, Font Awesome's CSS and
  each of its webfonts) has a sha256 in `app/ui/assets.py`, checked before anything is
  written to `vendor/`. A mismatch is a failed download (fatal on a first start, a
  warning that keeps the old files on an upgrade), and nothing from a failed run is
  written. `scripts/vendor_assets.py --check` re-hashes what is on disk and reports a
  `modified` file; `--print-hashes` produces the pins when bumping a version.
- **Dependencies:** bumped the locked packages the image scan flagged: anyio 4.15.1
  (CRITICAL, CVE-2026-63374), starlette 1.7.0 (CVE-2026-54283), python-multipart 0.0.32
  (CVE-2026-53539) and aiohttp 3.14.5 (CVE-2026-69244); typing-extensions and yarl move
  with them. On the new Starlette an over-long body sent without a `Content-Length` got
  a `500` instead of a `413`; the size cap now answers `413` whatever shape the overflow
  comes back to it in.

### Fixed

- **Queue outcomes never routed.** Enter Queue and Take From Queue read `queueResult`, a
  field Jambonz never sends (it sends `queue_result` and `dequeue_result`), so every
  outcome took `timeout`, a finished agent conversation included.
- **The Disconnect handler never ran, and Send SMS in Disconnect or Call Status never
  sent**: Jambonz has no disconnect hook and ignores the answer to a status hook.
- **The Call Status handler ran for every leg**, so a "post the call record" HTTP node
  fired several times per call.
- **The AI Agent sent an `llm` verb that no vendor accepts**, and the call dropped.
- **Template conditions written as `{{x}} == 'y'` were always true**; an empty input
  passed "less than"; a compare couldn't test one variable against another.
- **A Subflow never returned**; a cycle through a subflow or loop compiled cleanly, and the
  iteration cap then played thousands of prompts; a Loop left through a branch read as
  exhausted when entered again.
- **One slow API dropped the call** before the Error handler could answer.
- **The Jambonz portal rejected the env-var schema**, and it was unreachable behind
  webhook basic auth.
- **A call created over the REST API lost its customerData** at the first gather.
- **Misrouted answers:** a speech-recognizer error was a silent timeout, a low-confidence
  transcript a match, User Input below its minimum an answer, and a dial ending while
  ringing a failure.
- **Date/Time:** overnight windows were checked against the wrong day; an unknown timezone
  fell back to the host's local time.
- **Play Prompt:** loop 0 played once; the style prompt never reached anything that reads
  it. **Call Settings** with only a voice sent a synthesizer without a vendor, which
  Jambonz refuses, a blank language or voice cleared the call's, and it switched off the
  application's TTS fallback.
- **A prompt with its own voice or recognizer, or a Call Settings, switched the call to the
  vendor's unlabelled speech credential.** The application's credential labels are now
  read from the call's first hook and kept on every synthesizer and recognizer that uses
  the call's vendor.
- **A queue's wait subflow could silence the hold music**; a successful Blind Transfer
  still ran its fallback components.
- **The documented backup failed every time** (it couldn't read the session key) and
  left the app stopped.
- **A save on a full disk answered 500 though it had landed**, with no audit line, and
  `/health` said ok while saves failed.
- **`LOG_FORMAT=json` wasn't all JSON**; the session-key warning fired on read-only
  volumes; directory changes and deletes weren't durable.
- **Docs that no longer matched the code:** the hook model, trusted-header auth, the audit
  trail, `/health`, the masked-header list.
- **Deployment:** compose silently ignored most of `.env`. It listed settings one by one
  under `environment:`, so a dozen of them (among others `MAX_HOOK_SECONDS`,
  `HTTP_REQUEST_ALLOW_PRIVATE`, `CALL_TRACE_ENABLED`, `TRUSTED_USER_HEADER`, `LOG_LEVEL`,
  `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE`) never reached the container. The whole `.env` now goes in
  through `env_file` (optional, so the quick start still runs without one); only
  `STORE_DIR`, `DEBUG`, `UVICORN_WORKERS`, `APP_HOST` and `APP_PORT` are pinned.
  **Check your `.env`**: values that used to be ignored now take effect.
- **Deployment:** a restart cut off running webhooks. uvicorn now drains for up to
  `GRACEFUL_SHUTDOWN_SECONDS` (default 40, longer than `MAX_HOOK_SECONDS`) after
  `SIGTERM`, and compose waits 45 s (`stop_grace_period`) before it kills the
  container (Docker's default was 10 s).
- **Docs:** removed the claim that extra replicas can serve webhooks from a copy of the
  store: a copy is a separate, writable installation. One instance per store; high
  availability is a future platform concern.
- **Docs:** `docs/PLATFORM-HANDOFF.md` and `docs/ARCHITECTURE-DIRECTION.md` no longer
  describe groups, `/webhooks/{group}/{flow}` or basic auth for the editor.
- **A save could take a flow off the air**, two ways: it deleted the compiled artifact
  before recompiling outside the lock (a call in that gap hung up), and its check
  skipped the verb-schema validation the compile then failed. Every write now compiles
  first and replaces the artifact atomically in the same locked write.
- **The compiled artifact heals.** Missing, corrupt or from another release, it is
  rebuilt from the flow on the next call; a corrupt one used to be a 500 on every call.
- **One bad file no longer breaks the rest:** an invalid flow document is skipped (and
  logged) in the dashboard and `GET /api/flows`, an invalid snapshot no longer blocks
  saves or the history, and a short write on a full disk is completed rather than
  renamed over the good file.
- **A webhook could answer 500 and drop the call** on a `NaN`/`Infinity` (from an API
  response or a number env var); responses are now rendered where a failure still
  becomes a 200 with a hangup.
- **Large call state dropped the call:** variables near 1 MiB made Jambonz's next
  webhook a 413. Over `MAX_CALL_STATE_BYTES` the Error handler runs instead.
- **HTTP Request could hold a call indefinitely**: `HTTP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT` was per read,
  so a trickling upstream never timed out, and DNS had no bound with the SSRF guard
  off. It is now a total deadline, DNS included.
- **HTTP Request failed in bursts:** more than four requests resolving a hostname at
  once failed with "all 4 DNS lookup slots are still occupied", with the SSRF guard on
  before this release, and in every mode once DNS moved onto the bounded resolver. Only
  lookups abandoned to a hung resolver are capped now; every other lookup gets a thread.
- **A base URL in a placeholder broke the request:** with URL encoding,
  `{{env_vars.BASE}}{{path}}` encoded the path into the host
  (`https://api.example.com%2Fv1%2Fcustomers`). Where a URL's host part ends is now
  decided with the base's value in place, for the request and its log line alike, and a
  save warns about the two shapes the encoding changes (see Upgrade notes).
- **A variable name that wasn't text made a save a 500:** a number where a name belongs
  (`"variable_name": 7`, a Loop counter, a mapping's `variable`) or a non-list mapping
  in an imported flow made save, validate and import answer 500, and the webhook's
  rebuild of the flow fail. Names are read as text now; a Change Variable `operation`
  that isn't one is a 422 ("unknown operation") instead of a 500.
- **Load shedding didn't shed:** a burst saw free slots, then queued. Slots are now
  taken before the hook is admitted.
- **A field of the wrong type was a 500** on save, import and validate (a list as a
  Connector target, a number as an SMS recipient, …); the compiler now refuses the
  flow with an issue instead of raising.
- **Unknown webhook names cost a full store scan each**; misses are cached briefly.
- **Saves and Simulate blocked every webhook** while they ran; they now run off the
  event loop.
- **Resumes broke** for a subflow name or component id with `/`, `?`, `#` or a space,
  and a variable named like a gather result (`digits`…) made a later timeout read the
  stale value as an answer. Both are now refused at save.
- **The JSON Parser node had no icon**: `fa-brackets-curly` is a Font Awesome Pro icon,
  so the palette and its cards showed a blank. It now uses `fa-code`.
